notes: Five ui-specs (split the PAR HUD, the two patch-cell surfaces, the day-open cutscene, and the day-close regen feedback into separate testable items) plus three sfx presets. Zero art orders filed, per the brief's zero art budget. No music-brief item, per the brief's explicit 'no new music track'. State-surface assumptions the specs depend on, flagged so the Orchestrator can wire them alongside the engine changes already described in BRIEF.md: DuelState gains `par` (int) and `rotationsUsed` (int, incremented only on the player's `rotate` action, never on casts or patch-cell placements); DuelState/RunKit gains a patch-cell held count (0-3) and a per-turn `usedPatchCell` flag; RunState gains `lastRegen` (0-10, the actual amount just auto-restored at day close, for the animate-from value). The day-open-cutscene spec renders the narrative-director's `day-open-<n>` scene items (id pattern per BRIEF.md), `day-open-10` replacing FinalePre's hardcoded morning copy. Reused existing palette/idiom throughout: gold (`--kp-gold`) for all player-cast targeting affordances (already the ability-arming/targetbar color), the pip + `kp-banked-pop` primitives for new resource counters, and screen-shake reserved for combat impacts only (patch-cell placement and day-close regen get pulse/pop feedback, never shake).

items.spec: Add a PAR readout to the duel top bar (`.kp-dive2-osk`), placed immediately to the left of the existing STRAIN widget so the causal link ('this is what costs you strain') reads left-to-right. New element: `.kp-par` (flex, gap 6px, font-size 11px, letter-spacing .12em, color var(--kp-dim), matching the existing `.kp-duel-round`/`.kp-strain` treatment), title attribute 'Every rotation past PAR costs strain on a win.' Markup: `PAR{par}` (em = var(--kp-steel), the static budget) then `{rotationsUsed}` (the live counter, default var(--kp-text)). While rotationsUsed <= par this is the whole widget. The instant rotationsUsed increments past par (first over-par rotation), add class `kp-par-over` to `.kp-par`: `em`/`b` flip to var(--kp-crimson), and append `+{rotationsUsed - par} OVER` styled like `.kp-prog-tier` (kp-display, 9px, crimson instead of gold). The crossing moment (and only that moment) plays a one-shot `kp-par-warn-pop` animation (steps(4) 180ms scale from 1.5 to 1, same shape as the existing `kp-banked-pop`/`kp-claim-in` family) -- implement by bumping a ref-tracked `overParFlashKey` counter exactly once when the over-par boolean flips false to true, and keying the pop class off that counter so subsequent over-par rotations update the number live without re-popping. rotationsUsed and par are read-only display state computed by the engine; do not derive rotationsUsed client-side from RAM spend, since patch-cell placements also cost RAM but are not rotations.
acceptance: During phase 'playing', the top bar shows PAR and the live rotation count as one `.kp-par` widget positioned directly left of the STRAIN meter.
While rotationsUsed <= par, `.kp-par` shows no `kp-par-over` class, no crimson, no OVER tag, and never animates.
The exact rotation where rotationsUsed first exceeds par adds `kp-par-over` (crimson em/b) and plays the `kp-par-warn-pop` 180ms steps(4) scale-pop exactly once for the rest of the duel.
Every subsequent over-par rotation updates the `+{n} OVER` tag's number live without re-triggering the pop animation.
The widget and its crimson state remain visible for one readable beat under the win/lose overlay's fade-in, i.e. it is not hidden or reset before `.kp-overlay` covers the board.

items.spec: In `UpgradeScreen` (day close), add a second row beneath the existing NIGHT PATCH `.kp-patchrow`, reusing that same row's layout: `.kp-patchrow.kp-cellrow` containing a button 'BUY PATCH CELL (35 cr)' and a 3-slot pip readout. Button disables (opacity .4, same as `.kp-btn-ghost:disabled`) when credits < 35 or held === 3; its title attribute reads 'NEED 35 CR' or 'HOLDING MAX (3)' respectively so the disabled reason is legible on hover. On a successful buy: deduct 35 cr, increment held (max 3), play the existing `granted` preset on the `ui` bus (reuse, no new sfx needed here), and the next empty pip in the readout fills using the existing `kp-banked-pop` 300ms steps(3) scale-in. The pip readout is new: `.kp-cell-pips` (flex, gap 5px, 3 fixed `.kp-pip`-sized squares always rendered regardless of held count) with a new modifier `.kp-cell-pip-on` (background/border var(--kp-gold), matching the gold used for banked-RAM and program-tier chrome -- distinct from the RAM pips' signal/cream `.kp-pip-on` so the two resources never look interchangeable). Label text 'PATCH CELLS {held}/3' sits left of the pips, same `.kp-rail-dim` treatment as the existing STRAIN/credits line below it.
acceptance: UpgradeScreen shows a `.kp-cellrow` beneath the NIGHT PATCH row with a buy button and a 3-slot pip readout labeled PATCH CELLS {held}/3.
The buy button is disabled with title 'NEED 35 CR' when credits < 35, and with title 'HOLDING MAX (3)' when held === 3, and is otherwise clickable.
A successful purchase deducts 35 cr, increments held by exactly 1, plays `granted` on the ui bus, and the newly-filled pip uses the `kp-banked-pop` entrance.
The pip row always renders exactly 3 slots; filled slots use `.kp-cell-pip-on` (gold), never the RAM pip's signal color.
Held patch-cell count persists across days within a run (it is not reset at day close) until spent in a dive.

items.spec: Add a 4th dock button to `.kp-dock-abilities` alongside SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND: `.kp-ability.kp-prog-patch`, name 'PATCH CELL', meta '{held}/3 - 1R' (or 'NONE HELD' when held is 0, styled like an offline program). Clicking it (only when held > 0, not used this turn, and player's turn) arms targeting through the exact same `Targeting` flow already used for ATTACK/DEFEND in duel.tsx: opens `.kp-targetbar` reading 'PATCH CELL: pick 1 target' with the existing CANCEL (ESC) control, and adds `kp-ability-arming` to the button. While armed, legal cells are restricted to slag blocks (`kind === 'block'`) within the player's reach (same reach concept already used for free rotation); render their legal-ring in gold instead of the default cream by adding a new class `.kp-dblock-patchable` (copy of `.kp-dlegal-ring` geometry, stroke var(--kp-gold), same `kp-legal-pulse` steps(2) 1s animation) -- gold because this is a program cast in progress, matching the gold already used for `.kp-ability-arming`/`.kp-targetbar`/`.kp-rail-intent`, not a plain rotate target. If zero blocks are in reach when armed, still open the targetbar (so CANCEL/ESC stays available) with text 'PATCH CELL: no slag block in reach' and no board highlights, rather than silently failing to arm. Confirming a target: deduct 1 RAM, set the per-turn `usedPatchCell` flag (button meta becomes '... - USED' for the rest of the turn, same suffix pattern as the other three programs), convert the cell in place from a slag block to an open cross node (all four arms, unowned) using the existing `.kp-claimpop` 240ms steps(4) pop-in for the new node glyph, play the new `patchPlace` sfx on the game bus at that instant, and show a `CELL PLACED` `.kp-pulse-info` banner (same family as the existing SCANNED/DEFUSED/WARDED pulses). No screen shake: this is a utility placement, not a combat impact, and shake stays reserved for trap/siphon/turn-lost/win-lose/redirect so the telegraph vocabulary does not get diluted. After conversion the cell renders exactly like any other never-claimed open node; nothing about its later rendering marks it as former slag.
acceptance: With held > 0 and it is the player's turn, the dock shows a 4th button PATCH CELL with meta '{held}/3 - 1R'; with held === 0 it renders disabled with meta 'NONE HELD'.
Clicking it arms targeting identically to ATTACK/DEFEND: `.kp-ability-arming` on the button, `.kp-targetbar` open with a CANCEL (ESC) control.
While armed, only in-reach slag blocks show the gold `.kp-dblock-patchable` ring; no node, port, or core cell is selectable for this cast.
If no block is in reach, the targetbar still opens with 'PATCH CELL: no slag block in reach' and CANCEL remains usable; nothing on the board is highlighted.

Confirming a target deducts 1 RAM, flips the per-turn used flag (meta gains ' - USED'), converts the block to an open cross node with the `.kp-claimpop` entrance, plays `patchPlace` on the game bus, shows a `CELL PLACED` info pulse, and triggers zero screen shake.
Held count decrements immediately in both the dock meta and (next visit) the day-close pip readout from patchcell-dayclose-row.

items.spec: Introduce a `dayOpen` run-screen state that renders through the existing `StoryScene` component unchanged in its core interaction (click-anywhere-or-NEXT to advance, `story` sfx per beat on the ui bus, `.kp-story-beat` 160ms steps(3) entrance) -- reusing the same component the run opener/ender and tutorial-intro/outro already use. It plays once, immediately before the `day` screen (JobBoard) mounts, for every day 1-10, rendering the narrative-director's `day-open-<n>` scene item for the corresponding day n (id pattern per BRIEF.md); day 10's `day-open-10` scene replaces the hardcoded copy block currently in `FinalePre` ('No tickets today. The counter is dark...') as the day-10 morning frame -- remove that static paragraph once this is wired. Two additions on top of the shared component: (1) a fixed top-left `.kp-story-daytag` reading 'DAY {n}' (kp-display font, 10px, var(--kp-gold), 2px border chrome matching `.kp-window-title`'s weight) present for the entire scene regardless of which beat is showing -- this is the one piece of chrome that tells the player 'this is a day-open beat', independent of the dialogue copy; tutorial-intro/outro and the run opener/ender do not get this tag. (2) `windowTitle()` gets a `dayOpen` case returning 'MORNING.LOG', distinct from 'SHOPFRONT' (run boundary) and 'JOBS.QUE' (job board itself). `dayOpen` is added to the unclosable-screen set (same treatment as `opener`): the flow window's close control is a no-op while it is showing, since it is a mandatory beat, not a dismissable one. Finishing the last beat transitions straight to the `day` screen with no intermediate frame, and the scene does not replay on returning to the job board later that same day.
acceptance: A day-open scene uses the exact same StoryScene click/NEXT-to-advance interaction and `story` sfx as the run opener; nothing about the base component changes.
A persistent `.kp-story-daytag` reading 'DAY {n}' in gold kp-display text is visible across every beat of a day-open scene, and is absent from opener/ender/tutorial scenes.
The flow window title reads 'MORNING.LOG' while screen is `dayOpen`; its close control is inert while that screen is active.
Completing the final beat lands directly on the job board with no flash of the prior screen.
Day 10's day-open scene (badge 'DAY 10') fully replaces FinalePre's static two-paragraph copy; FinalePre keeps only its CONFIGURE KIT / OPEN THE BACK ROOM actions.

items.spec: On `UpgradeScreen`, surface the +10 (cap 100) auto-regen as a visible, once-per-mount animation instead of a silent number change. Add `.kp-regen` above the upgrade grid: the existing `.kp-strain-bar`/`.kp-strain-fill` meter (already used in the duel header, `width 300ms steps(6)` transition) plus a 'STRAIN' label. This screen depends on the reducer exposing `lastRegen` (0-10, the amount actually just granted this close -- 0 if strain was already capped before regen). On mount: render the bar pre-filled at `strain - lastRegen`; after a 150ms hold (matching the window-open beat elsewhere in this codebase), animate the fill to `strain` via the existing steps(6) transition, and at that same 150ms mark play the new `dayCloseRegen` sfx on the ui bus and pop in a `+{lastRegen} STRAIN` tag using the existing `kp-banked-pop` 300ms steps(3) treatment (reuse verbatim, do not invent a new pop). When `lastRegen` is 0, skip all of it: render the bar statically at its resting value with no fill animation, no pop tag, and no sfx -- a maxed bar never fakes a gain. This fires once per day-close mount only (UpgradeScreen is not remounted between upgrade-button clicks and the day transition, so a normal `useEffect` on mount is sufficient). Small adjacent fix while touching this screen: the NIGHT PATCH purchase button currently dispatches with no audio at all; wire its existing click handler to also play the existing `granted` preset on the ui bus (no new sfx needed) so every credit spend on this screen has a voice.
acceptance: UpgradeScreen shows a strain meter above the upgrade grid that, on mount, visibly fills from `strain - lastRegen` to `strain` using the existing 300ms steps(6) transition, starting after a 150ms hold.
The `dayCloseRegen` sfx plays exactly once per mount, timed to the start of that fill, on the ui bus.
A `+{lastRegen} STRAIN` tag pops in using the existing `kp-banked-pop` animation, synced to the same 150ms mark.
When lastRegen is 0, the meter renders at its resting value with no animation, no pop, and no sfx.
Clicking NIGHT PATCH now plays the existing `granted` preset on the ui bus in addition to its current effect.

items.when: The instant a targeted slag block finishes converting into an open cross junction (patch-cell placement confirmed via the duel dock's PATCH CELL cast). A mechanical unfold: square wave, rising arp, close cousin of the existing `unlock` preset but shorter, reading as 'a door opening' rather than 'a program unlocked'.

Every player rotation once rotationsUsed exceeds par, including the rotation that first crosses the threshold. A short noise click, deliberately quiet and short since it can repeat many times in a row; call it with jitter around 0.05 (via the existing `sfx()` opts) so a run of over-par rotations does not read as a metronome. Layers on top of the existing `rotate` sfx already played for every rotation; it does not replace it.

On UpgradeScreen (day close), the moment the strain meter begins its auto-regen fill animation (once per mount, skipped entirely when lastRegen is 0). A warm sine swell with a light upward vibrato, reading as 'restorative' rather than the sharper transactional feel of `granted`.
